questions.q: Why does this lesson say a configured failover group is still 'just a theory' until tested?
options: Because failover groups expire after 30 days if untested
Because Azure requires a separate certification process
Because a mechanism that's configured and a mechanism that's proven to work are different things — a DR plan nobody has ever triggered is a plan on paper, not a tested capability
Because testing is required by Azure before billing starts
questions.explain: This is exactly the gap the board's mandate would fail against if left unaddressed — hence testing it deliberately before Chapter 7's unannounced drill.

questions.q: Against which server is `Switch-AzSqlDatabaseFailoverGroup` actually run to trigger a manual failover?
options: Both servers simultaneously
The secondary server — you're telling the secondary to become the new primary, not telling the primary to step down
The primary server, telling it to step down
Neither — it's run against the resource group itself
questions.explain: The real syntax runs this cmdlet against the secondary server's name, reflecting what's actually happening: the secondary being promoted.

questions.q: What is the real step that makes the failover group 'worth building,' according to this lesson's description of what happens during failover?
options: The secondary being promoted to primary
A new backup being taken
The old primary being deleted
The listener endpoint being automatically repointed to the new primary, so the application doesn't need to be told anything
questions.explain: The automatic endpoint repoint is exactly the capability Lesson 12 built the failover group to provide.

questions.q: What should actually be checked during a failover test, beyond whether the command succeeded?
options: Only the billing cost of the failover
Only whether the old primary still exists
Nothing else — a successful command is sufficient

How long the application was unreachable (vs. the RTO target), whether in-flight writes were lost (vs. the RPO target), whether the app reconnected automatically, and whether data on the new primary is correct
questions.explain: A real pass measures actual downtime and data loss against the planned RPO/RTO targets, confirms automatic reconnection, and verifies data correctness.

questions.q: If the application does NOT reconnect automatically after the listener endpoint repoints, what does this lesson say that indicates?
options: A gap in the application's own retry logic, not a failure of the failover group itself
The RPO target was missed
The test should be considered a complete success regardless
The failover group itself is broken and must be rebuilt
questions.explain: The failover group's job is repointing the endpoint — whether the application reconnects on its own is a separate concern about the app's retry logic.
